summary: RFC 6514 created a space of Tunnel Type code points for the BGP PMSI Tunnel attribute but no IANA registry for it. This document updates RFC 6514 to create that registry so further values can be allocated.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 7385 creates an IANA registry for tunnel types used by the BGP PMSI Tunnel attribute. It lists the original values and defines how other code points are handled.

subtitle: Creates an IANA registry for BGP PMSI tunnel type code points.

tldr.problem: RFC 6514 defined PMSI Tunnel Type code points but did not create an IANA registry for assigning additional values.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7385 creates a registry in the BGP Parameters registry and sets allocation rules for the code-point ranges.
tldr.outcome: RFC 7385 updates RFC 6514 and was later updated by RFC 8317 and RFC 8338.

today: RFC 7385 updates RFC 6514 and was later updated by RFC 8317 and RFC 8338.

sections.title: A Registry for PMSI Tunnel Types
sections.content:
RFC 6514 defines an octet field for the tunnel type in the P-Multicast Service Interface (PMSI) Tunnel attribute. It allocated values 0 through 7 but did not create a corresponding IANA registry.

RFC 7385 creates the registry because further code-point allocations were needed, including one for Inter-Area P2MP Segmented LSPs.
sections.plainLanguage: The earlier specification assigned tunnel-type values but did not provide an official registry for new assignments. This RFC creates that registry.

sections.title: Allocation Rules and Initial Values
sections.content:
IANA creates the P-Multicast Service Interface Tunnel (PMSI Tunnel) Tunnel Types registry within the BGP Parameters registry. The values from 0x00 through 0xFA use IETF Review. Values 0xFB through 0xFE are experimental and are not assigned. Value 0xFF is reserved and can change status only through Standards Action.

The initial registry lists the values from RFC 6514, covering no tunnel information, RSVP-TE P2MP LSP, mLDP P2MP LSP, PIM trees, ingress replication, and mLDP MP2MP LSP. Values 0x08 through 0xFA are unassigned.
sections.plainLanguage: The registry records the existing tunnel types and leaves a range available for future assignments. Separate ranges are reserved for experiments and for a reserved code point.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC says it simply creates an IANA registry from a table in RFC 6514 and therefore has no security concerns.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC says its registry change introduces no security concerns.
